issues.failure_explanation: The bound on the weighted PDE residual of (u_eps, f_eps) is P/sqrt|Q_T| times the norms of the differences u-u_eps and f-f_eps. That presumes the weighted residual of the exact pair (u,f) vanishes. With independent weights it does not: if phi_{theta^1} is identically 2 and all other weights are identically 1, the residual of (u,f) is d_t u, which is nonzero. The same happens in the initial and terminal terms, where (phi_6-phi_7)u_0 is nonzero when phi_6 differs from phi_7. The theorem quantifies over arbitrary bounded weights, so it is false as stated. Moreover, the adversarial maximum over the weights, which is what the method actually trains, is not small for the exact solution: raising one weight by s gives roughly s^2||d_t u||^2 - rho s^2. The same argument is reused for the wave and bilinear versions.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that the WeightedPINN loss can be made small by increasing width and depth holds only for the unweighted case, or for weights tied together so that the exact residual vanishes. It is unsupported for general adaptive weights, and for the min-max objective.

issues.failure_explanation: u_eps and f_eps are functions of (t,x) in R^{d+1}, and the networks u_theta and phi_theta are defined on R^{d+1}. The invoked approximation result (stated in the commented-out lemma with exponent -2(n-m)/d, where d is the input dimension) therefore applies with d+1 in place of d. The rates W^{-2/d}L^{-2/d}, W^{-4/d}L^{-4/d}, the threshold W^{1/d}L^{1/d} >= eps^{-(d+7)/2}, and the final rate W^{-1/d}L^{-1/d} are all misstated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace d by d+1 in the exponents and in the threshold relating W, L and eps, and restate the rate as (WL)^{-1/(d+1)}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence rate in width and depth is too optimistic. The correct exponent is 1/(d+1), and the regime condition on W and L changes accordingly.
issues.title: Approximation rates use the spatial dimension d although the approximated functions live in d+1 variables
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and the argument structure survives, but the headline rate is weakened, so it is more than a routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem concludes that ||f-f_theta||_{L^2(q_T)} and ||u-u_theta|| are O(delta) for the given control f. The exact control is not unique. Take any w in C_c^infty(q_T). Then u'=u+w satisfies the equation with control f'=f+(d_t w-Delta w+v(u+w)-v(u)) supported in omega, and has the same u(0) and u(T). The pair (u',f') has zero loss, yet ||f'-f|| and ||u'-u|| are fixed positive numbers. The proof applies the cost estimate of the cited controllability theorem to the specific difference f-f_theta, but that estimate bounds the minimal-norm control, not an arbitrary control steering the difference equation to zero. The same applies to the wave version.

issues.failure_explanation: ū is defined by the forward heat equation with terminal data ū(T)=z_0 in L^2, i.e. a backward heat problem. Such a problem has no solution for general L^2 data, so ū is not well defined. The estimate eq:energy has the form y' + a <= C y + g, which yields forward Gronwall bounds in terms of y(0). The proof instead derives y(t) <= e^{C(T-t)}(y(T)+...), which would require the opposite inequality. Counterexample: with R=0, V=0, û(T)=eps sin(k pi x), the solution is û(t)=eps e^{k^2 pi^2 (T-t)} sin(k pi x), so the bound on û(0) in terms of û(T) fails. The bound on û(0) is then used in eq:f_est1.

issues.failure_explanation: Integration by parts against û gives the boundary term ∫_{∂Ω} û (∇û·ν). Here û=u_theta−ū with ū=0 on Σ_T, so the trace of û is u_theta but ∇û·ν=∇u_theta·ν−∇ū·ν. The proof drops the ∇ū·ν contribution. This term is not controlled by the loss, and ū is only a weak solution with no normal-derivative trace. The wave proof has the same flaw with ∂_t û (∇û·ν). The residual-based bound on the boundary term is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle the boundary data via a lifting or by testing with a zero-trace function (for example, working with u_theta−ū−extension), and prove a stability lemma that does not need the normal derivative of ū.
issues.overall_effect: The estimates eq:energy, eq:hat_u_est1 and eq:hat_u_est2, and the final constants, are unjustified. This holds even if the other issues were repaired.
issues.title: Energy estimates replace the normal derivative of û on the boundary by that of u_theta
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma (a lifting argument) should restore the energy estimate without changing the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The center has norm 1/sqrt(d)≈0.316 for d=10, and the radius is 0.75. The point of the unit sphere in the direction of the center lies at distance 1−0.316=0.684<0.75 from it. That boundary point lies in the closed ball and hence in Ω∖ω, so ω does not contain ∂Ω or a neighbourhood of it. Assumption (A3), the hypothesis of the wave stability theorem, is therefore not satisfied, although the text says it is.
